watches.name: Navigator from Richard’s Own Collection
watches.description: This watch is Sold From my personal collection: a one-of-a-kind Navigator A Tribute to the German B-Uhr Sold out years ago. Now, my personal Navigator with distinctive red hands is available. FROM MY COLLECTION TO YOURS The Rpaige Navigator 1939 sold out years ago. Now, as I release a few watches from my personal collection, I’m offering something special: a one-of-a-kind Navigator with striking red hands. Those red hands give this watch its own personality—a vivid contrast against the black dial and luminous numerals. Paired with a brushed stainless steel case and warm tan leather strap, the result is bold, distinctive, and unmistakably Rpaige. At its heart is a historic vintage Swiss Phenix movement, made decades before the watch that now houses it. Manually wound and decorated with perlage, blue screws, and gold plating, it can be admired through the exhibition case back. The original Navigator was limited to just 20 pieces worldwide. This red-hand version is unique—and it comes directly from my own collection. The Navigator is a real tribute to the antique B-Uhr watches manufactured by several brands during Second World War, for German pilots. This exclusive 47mm watch, available in a extremely limited run of only 20 pieces, is clearly oriented to hardcore collectors and lovers of authentic pilot’s watches. It contains a Vintage Swiss “Phenix” movement, manufactured in 1935. case: Brushed Stainless Steel 316L, with glass front, and glass exhibition back. 47mm diameter. Dimensions: 47mm diameter, 56mm from lug to lug. 12.5mm thick. Movement: Vintage Swiss “Phenix” movement, manufactured in 1935. Special hand decorated and embellished with Perlage, blue screws, and gold plating. Manual Wind, Power Reserve 40h. Strap: Tan, thick, leather with white stitching. one year warranty.

watches.name: The Rpaige “Chrysler Building” – Blue Enamel Dial
watches.description: One of a kind in the World A Tribute to an American Icon The Rpaige, “Chrysler Building” Blue. This watch was five years in the making due to it’s complexity of design. The Chrysler Building has always been, to me, the apex of American Art Deco architectural design and a tribute to the American Automobile industry. Designed by William Van Allen, for the Chrysler Automobile Company, the building broke ground on September 19, 1928. When the Chrysler was finished in 1930, it was declared the world’s tallest building. The Chrysler Building is considered a leading example of Art Deco architecture. It is constructed of a steel frame in-filled with masonry, with areas of decorative metal cladding. Approximately fifty metal ornaments protrude at the building’s corners on five floors reminiscent of gargoyles on Gothic cathedrals.The 31st-floor contains gargoyles and replicas of the 1929 Chrysler radiator caps, the 61st floor – Eagles, a nod to America’s national bird. The building is also decorated with Chrysler Car hood ornaments. It is an iconic landmark in NYC, and renowned the world over. case: The Rpaige “Chrysler Building” watch is made of steel. It measures 44mm in diameter, 58mm in length, and 14mm thick, with sapphires crystals. It is water resistant to 50 meters The case takes its design lead from the Chrysler Building’s Art Deco crown. The building’s crown is composed of seven radiating terraced arches, with distinctive triangular windows. Each arch section is smaller and higher than the previous, giving the top of the building a wedding cake effect. At the base of the top part of the building lies the famous “Eagle gargoyles”. The watch case is a tribute to the crowning glory of the building’s majestic design. On one side is a tribute to the radiating arched terraced with triangular cut outs for the windows. The opposite side boldly integrates the “Eagle Gargoyles” into the watch lugs, using the Eagles eyes as the pin hole. Movement: 17 jewel, New, Swiss, DB6, brushed finished movement, Rhodium. Glucydur, 21’600, blue screws, skeletonized ratchet wheel. Dial: Dial: The dial on this one in the series is designed by Rpaige. It’s a tribute to the Art Deco Era, using the lines and principals from the 1920’s. The dial is a hand made blue fire enameled, with an Rpaige designed Art Deco styled chapter ring in blue and silver, with Art Deco Arabic numbers. The hands are Rpaige designed “Chrysler Building” style hands with chrome/white enamel and luminous. This watch is a one of a kind in the World. Shown with a blue genuine Ostrich leg strap with blue stitching.

Antique Sterling Silver and Rose gold “Niello” dial. White luminous hands. Niello is a black mixture, usually of sulphur, copper, silver, and lead, used as an inlay on engraved or etched metal, especially silver. It is added as a powder or paste, then fired until it melts or at least softens, and flows or is pushed into the engraved lines in the metal. It hardens and blackens when cool, and the niello on the flat surface is polished off to show the filled lines in black, contrasting with the polished metal around it. The contrast of the black niello against the bright silver surface produces an attractive decorative effect. Niello was used on a variety of objects over the ages, including sword hilts, chalices, plates, horns, adornment for horses, jewellery such as bracelets, rings, pendants, and small fittings such as strap-ends, buttons, belt buckles and especially on antique Pocket watch cases. Dimensions: 41mm wide, 12mm thick, 53mm end to end. Movement: 17 Jewel Chinese movement. Dial: Sterling silver antique “Niello” dial. Rpaige Chapter ring in black and Silver with Art Deco numbers. Green hands. Niello is a black mixture, usually of sulphur, copper, silver, and lead, used as an inlay on engraved or etched metal, especially silver. It is added as a powder or paste, then fired until it melts or at least softens, and flows or is pushed into the engraved lines in the metal. It hardens and blackens when cool, and the niello on the flat surface is polished off to show the filled lines in black, contrasting with the polished metal around it. The contrast of the black niello against the bright silver surface produces an attractive decorative effect. Niello was used on a variety of objects over the ages, including sword hilts, chalices, plates, horns, adornment for horses, jewellery such as bracelets, rings, pendants, and small fittings such as strap-ends, buttons, belt buckles and especially on antique Pocket watch cases. A Die-struck dial was made by this process: A master die was hand-engraved or etched by skilled artisans to include the intricate details, such as numbers, indices, logos, or patterns for the dial. This die acted as a stamp to transfer the design onto the blank watch dial. The creation of the die required precision since any flaw would be replicated on every dial. After striking, the raw dials were cleaned, smoothed, and refined to remove any burrs or rough edges left by the striking process. Hand finishing was often involved to enhance or deepen certain details. Weight: Steel Case – 82.7 grams Shown with a hand made blue Alligator skin strap. watches.name: The Rpaige “Chrysler Building” Special Edition 41mm
watches.description: This watch is Sold Number 2/5 in the edition A Tribute to an American Icon The Rpaige, limited edition of 5 series “Chrysler Building”. This watch was five years in the making due to it’s complexity of design. The Chrysler Building has always been, to me, the apex of American Art Deco architectural design and a tribute to the American Automobile industry. Designed by William Van Allen, for the Chrysler Automobile Company, the building broke ground on September 19, 1928. When the Chrysler was finished in 1930, it was declared the world’s tallest building. The Chrysler Building is considered a leading example of Art Deco architecture. It is constructed of a steel frame in-filled with masonry, with areas of decorative metal cladding. Approximately fifty metal ornaments protrude at the building’s corners on five floors reminiscent of gargoyles on Gothic cathedrals.The 31st-floor contains gargoyles and replicas of the 1929 Chrysler radiator caps, the 61st floor – Eagles, a nod to America’s national bird. The building is also decorated with Chrysler Car hood ornaments. It is an iconic landmark in NYC, and renowned the world over. There will only be five watches of this series made. Each one will be unique. Each one of the five will have a different dial. Each one will be numbered on the back on the case. case: The Rpaige “Chrysler Building” watch is made of steel. It measures 41mm in diameter, 57mm in length, and 13mm thick, with sapphires crystals. It is water resistant to 50 meters The case takes its design lead from the Chrysler Building’s Art Deco crown. The building’s crown is composed of seven radiating terraced arches, with distinctive triangular windows. Each arch section is smaller and higher than the previous, giving the top of the building a wedding cake effect. At the base of the top part of the building lies the famous “Eagle gargoyles”. The watch case is a tribute to the crowning glory of the building’s majestic design. On one side is a tribute to the radiating arched terraced with triangular cut outs for the windows. The opposite side boldly integrates the “Eagle Gargoyles” into the watch lugs, using the Eagles eyes as the pin hole. Movement: 17 jewel, New, Swiss, DB6, brushed finished movement. Dial: The dial on this first one in the series is an antique, from the 1920’s, Art Deco, sterling Silver dial with 14kt gold applied Art Deco numbers. The hands are Dauphin style beveled, with blue ION plating with luminous. The second hand is an antique blued steel. Shown with a blue genuine Ostrich strap.

Slight flaw on rim of seconds dial. Blue Cathedral style hands with luminous. Antique blued steel seconds hand. The Montgomery Safety Dial was invented by Henry S. Montgomery, the General Watch and Clock Inspector from 1896 to 1923 for the Santa Fe Railway. The Montgomery Dial featured an outer track with individual minutes numbered from 1 to 60. The dial first appeared around 1904, and was used across the entire Santa Fe Railway system to help ensure the safety of Santa Fe crew members and passengers. Santa Fe used mercury-pendulum regulators at all crew change points across the system for crewmen to set their pocket watches, and the Montgomery Safety Dial helped to ensure accurate time readings. Vermeil In olden times, the jewelers and craftsmen of metal dealt with the problem of silver oxidation when exposed to air, a chemical reaction that caused the corrosion of the precious mineral and consequently of the artwork. The solution was provided in the mid-eighteenth century by some French goldsmiths who, through a fire gilding, applied to the surface of silver a sheet of gold. The final outcome appeared as an object with bright gold finish – more precious than silver and with the typical benefits of gold. This process was called vermeil. Dimensions: 51mm diameter, 9mm thick. 16 size USA. Movement: 17 jewel Illinois Antique American pocket watch movement. Burlington Special. Manufactured in 1918 in Springfield, Illinois . Bimetallic balance wheel, Fancy Swan regulator. Adjusted. Rose gold train wheels. Geneva Stripe finish. Dial: Antique white fire enameled collectors, Burlington Special “Montgomery” dial with black Arabic Numbers, and minutes. Antique Blued steel hands. The Montgomery Safety Dial was invented by Henry S. Montgomery, the General Watch and Clock Inspector from 1896 to 1923 for the Santa Fe Railway. The Montgomery Dial featured an outer track with individual minutes numbered from 1 to 60. The dial first appeared around 1904, and was used across the entire Santa Fe Railway system to help ensure the safety of Santa Fe crew members and passengers. Santa Fe used mercury-pendulum regulators at all crew change points across the system for crewmen to set their pocket watches, and the Montgomery Safety Dial helped to ensure accurate time readings. one year warranty.

However, the Skyscraper case was engineered for a new Swiss Unitas/ETA movement and only 150 of these cases are available worldwide. To make the “Skyscraper” even more sought after and desirable, we designed a very limited edition of only 20 Art Deco inspired dials in engraved metal “the Broadway” edition. The “Broadway” dial is engraved in metal, and hand finished with midnight blue Art Deco numbers. Even at this size, the angled lugs and flat bottom make the watch sit snugly on even average to smaller wrists. The case is 316L Surgical Grade Stainless Steel. The watch features a sapphire crystal and an exhibition back which shows off the movement’s decoration. Water resistance is rated at 50 meters (150 feet). The watch is paired with a black leather strap with white stitching and each watch will be sent in a zippered travel case. This is your chance to own a true Masterpiece of Art Deco design as a modern wristwatch. The Skyscraper edition is limited to 150 watches worldwide, but the “Broadway” edition will only be a series of 20. The watches are numbered on the side of each case. Dial: Antique Sterling Silver “Niello” dial with inland “Iris Flowers” style design. Skeleton dial ring with roman numeral numbers – black and gold color. “Chrysler Building” style hands lack and chrome with luminous. Niello is a black mixture, usually of sulphur, copper, silver, and lead, used as an inlay on engraved or etched metal, especially silver. It is added as a powder or paste, then fired until it melts or at least softens, and flows or is pushed into the engraved lines in the metal. It hardens and blackens when cool, and the niello on the flat surface is polished off to show the filled lines in black, contrasting with the polished metal around it. The contrast of the black niello against the bright silver surface produces an attractive decorative effect. Niello was used on a variety of objects over the ages, including sword hilts, chalices, plates, horns, adornment for horses, jewellery such as bracelets, rings, pendants, and small fittings such as strap-ends, buttons, belt buckles and especially on antique Pocket watch cases. Weight: Steel Case – 82.7 grams Shown with brown genuine leather strap with tan contrast stitching. This watch is a one-off. it number #28/50 in the series. watches.name: The Rpaige “Chrysler Building” 3
watches.description: Rpaige Chrysler Building 3 A Tribute to an American Icon The Rpaige, very limited edition, “Chrysler Building”. This watch was three years in the making due to it’s complexity of design. The Chrysler Building has always been, to me, the apex of American Art Deco architectural design and a tribute to the American Automobile industry. Designed by William Van Allen, for the Chrysler Automobile Company, the building broke ground on September 19, 1928. When the Chrysler was finished in 1930, it was declared the world’s tallest building. The Chrysler Building is considered a leading example of Art Deco architecture. It is constructed of a steel frame in-filled with masonry, with areas of decorative metal cladding. Approximately fifty metal ornaments protrude at the building’s corners on five floors reminiscent of gargoyles on Gothic cathedrals.The 31st-floor contains gargoyles and replicas of the 1929 Chrysler radiator caps, the 61st floor – Eagles, a nod to America’s national bird. The building is also decorated with Chrysler Car hood ornaments. It is an iconic landmark in NYC, and renowned the world over. There will only be seven of these watches made, five of which will be for sale to the watch community. Two of the seven watches will go into my own collection. Each one unique in movement and dial. All of the seven watches will house an historic American antique pocket watch movement. Close-up of the Chrysler Building, New York City. case: The Rpaige “Chrysler Building” watch is a hand made steel prototype case. It measures 44mm in diameter, 58mm in length, and 14mm thick, with sapphires crystals. It is water resistant to 50 meters The case takes it’s design lead from the Chrysler Building’s Art Deco crown. The building’s crown is composed of seven radiating terraced arches, with distinctive triangular windows. Each arch section is smaller and higher than the previous, giving the top of the building a wedding cake effect. At the base of the top part of the building lies the famous “Eagle gargoyles”. The watch case is a tribute to the crowning glory of the building’s majestic design. On one side is a tribute to the radiating arched terraced with triangular cut outs for the windows. The opposite side boldly integrates the “Eagle Gargoyles” into the watch lugs, using the Eagles eyes as the pin hole. Movement: All of the seven watches will house antique, historic and rare, 12 size, American pocket watch movements. The 3rd in this series houses a High grade 19 Jewel “Riverside” 12 size Waltham USA pocket watch movement. This movement was hand assembled in 1904 at the Waltham Factory in Waltham, Massachusetts. It contains rose gold jewel cups, rose gold train wheels, rose gold timing screws. The watch is “adjusted”. It has a fancy “Star” regulator, and an exceptional finish. Dial: The dial is an antique, rare, mint condition, fire enameled on copper in white. The numbers are the original luminous finish Arabic numbers.

watches.name: The Rpaige “Chrysler Building”
watches.description: This watch is Sold Rpaige Chrysler Building A Tribute to an American Icon The Rpaige, very limited edition, “Chrysler Building”. This watch was three years in the making due to it’s complexity of design. The Chrysler Building has always been, to me, the apex of American Art Deco architectural design and a tribute to the American Automobile industry. Designed by William Van Allen, for the Chrysler Automobile Company, the building broke ground on September 19, 1928. When the Chrysler was finished in 1930, it was declared the world’s tallest building. The Chrysler Building is considered a leading example of Art Deco architecture. It is constructed of a steel frame in-filled with masonry, with areas of decorative metal cladding. Approximately fifty metal ornaments protrude at the building’s corners on five floors reminiscent of gargoyles on Gothic cathedrals.The 31st-floor contains gargoyles and replicas of the 1929 Chrysler radiator caps, the 61st floor – Eagles, a nod to America’s national bird. The building is also decorated with Chrysler Car hood ornaments. It is an iconic landmark in NYC, and renowned the world over. There will only be seven of these watches made, five of which will be for sale to the watch community. Two of the seven watches will go into my own collection. Each one unique in movement and dial. All of the seven watches will house an historic American antique pocket watch movement. Close-up of the Chrysler Building, New York City. case: The Rpaige “Chrysler Building” watch is a hand made steel prototype case. It measures 44mm in diameter, 58mm in length, and 14mm thick, with sapphires crystals. It is water resistant to 50 meters The case takes it’s design lead from the Chrysler Building’s Art Deco crown. The building’s crown is composed of seven radiating terraced arches, with distinctive triangular windows. Each arch section is smaller and higher than the previous, giving the top of the building a wedding cake effect. At the base of the top part of the building lies the famous “Eagle gargoyles”. The watch case is a tribute to the crowning glory of the building’s majestic design. On one side is a tribute to the radiating arched terraced with triangular cut outs for the windows. The opposite side boldly integrates the “Eagle Gargoyles” into the watch lugs, using the Eagles eyes as the pin hole. Movement: All of the seven watches will house antique, historic and rare, 12 size, American pocket watch movements. The first in this series houses the “Holy Grail” of 12 size Waltham USA pocket watch movements: the 23 jewel “Riverside Maximus”. This movement was hand assembled in 1903 at the Waltham Factory in Waltham, Massachusetts. It contains rose gold jewel cups, rose gold train wheels, rose gold timing screws, and a rose gold cap jewel on the pallet bridge.The train jewels are rubies, and the cap jewels on the escape wheel and the balance cap jewel are made of a rose cut genuine diamonds. It has a fancy “Star” regulator, and an exceptional finish. Dial: The dial is an antique, rare, mint condition, fire enameled on copper in white. The numbers are black Roman Numeral fired into the enamel. At each number is a raised black glass bead fired enameled into the dial.

Floral Motif, with rose colored Rpaige chapter ring with Roman Numerals. Blue enameled “block form” hands with luminous. Niello is a black mixture, usually of sulphur, copper, silver, and lead, used as an inlay on engraved or etched metal, especially silver and gold. It is added as a powder or paste, then fired until it melts or at least softens, and flows or is pushed into the engraved lines in the metal. It hardens and blackens when cool, and the niello on the flat surface is polished off to show the filled lines in black, contrasting with the polished metal around it. The contrast of the black niello against the bright silver surface produces an attractive decorative effect. Niello was used on a variety of objects over the ages, including sword hilts, chalices, plates, horns, adornment for horses, jewellery such as bracelets, rings, pendants, and small fittings such as strap-ends, buttons, belt buckles and especially on antique Pocket watch cases. watches.description: This watch is Sold Vintage Elgin USA Movement from 1926 case: Titanium with Convex sapphire crystal front, diamond coated glass display back. Water Resistant to 50 meters (150 feet). “Helmet” style Rpaige Crown. Dimensions: 44mm diameter, 14mm thick, 52 mm end to end. Water resistant to 50 meters. Oversize Rpaige crown. Movement: 17 jewel Elgin USA movement. Manufactured in Elgin, Illinois in 1926. Adjusted to 3 positions. Dial: Antique Sterling Silver “Niello” dial with scene of horse and horseman in the forest. Niello is a black mixture, usually of sulphur, copper, silver, and lead, used as an inlay on engraved or etched metal, especially silver. It is added as a powder or paste, then fired until it melts or at least softens, and flows or is pushed into the engraved lines in the metal. It hardens and blackens when cool, and the niello on the flat surface is polished off to show the filled lines in black, contrasting with the polished metal around it. The contrast of the black niello against the bright silver surface produces an attractive decorative effect. Niello was used on a variety of objects over the ages, including sword hilts, chalices, plates, horns, adornment for horses, jewellery such as bracelets, rings, pendants, and small fittings such as strap-ends, buttons, belt buckles and especially on antique Pocket watch cases. Weight: Titanium Case – 65.7 grams Shown with custom Hand made grey Crocodile strap with blue stitching. This watch is a One of a Kind in the World All Rpaige watches come with a one year warranty.

It hardens and blackens when cool, and the niello on the flat surface is polished off to show the filled lines in black, contrasting with the polished metal around it. The contrast of the black niello against the bright silver surface produces an attractive decorative effect. Niello was used on a variety of objects over the ages, including sword hilts, chalices, plates, horns, adornment for horses, jewellery such as bracelets, rings, pendants, and small fittings such as strap-ends, buttons, belt buckles and especially on antique Pocket watch cases. Weight: Steel Case – 82.7 grams Shown with a blue genuine Crocodile strap, handmade. This watch is a one-off, it is number #12/50 in the series. Each watch in this series will be unique. Hard to see with the naked eye. Original blued steel “Spear” hands with red enamel tips. The Montgomery Safety Dial was invented by Henry S. Montgomery, the General Watch and Clock Inspector from 1896 to 1923 for the Santa Fe Railway. The Montgomery Dial featured an outer track with individual minutes numbered from 1 to 60. The dial first appeared around 1904, and was used across the entire Santa Fe Railway system to help ensure the safety of Santa Fe crew members and passengers. Santa Fe used mercury-pendulum regulators at all crew change points across the system for crewmen to set their pocket watches, and the Montgomery Safety Dial helped to ensure accurate time readings. A “true” Montgomery dial has the “6” inside the seconds bit. Shown with a matte black crocodile strap, made in Italy This watch is One-of-a-Kind. All Rpaige watches come with a one year warranty.

Art Deco was the design of the era, and is reflected in architecture (Empire State Building, Chrysler Building), art (Picasso), and fashion. Dimensions: 44mm wide, 13.5 mm thick, 56 mm end to end. Movement: Very high Grade, 19 jewel antique Gruen “Precision” Chronometer. Manufactured in 1915 in Switzerland. Adjusted to 5 positions. Rose gold train wheels, rose gold balance screws. Fancy screw calibrater regulator. The Gruen Watch Company was one of the premiere American watch manufactures. They were headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio. The Gruen's made the decision in the early 1900's to set up a factory in Biel, Switzerland to take advantage of the highly skilled watchmakers of the region. The highest quality Gruen movements were produced in this factory, and only the better quality caliber's were marked “Precision” on the dial and movement. These watchmaking gems were then sent back to the Ohio factory for casing and distribution. Dial: Original Gruen “Precision” dial made in Switzerland. Beautifully engraved sterling silver, with applied roman numeral numbers. the dial was then gold “Vermeil”. Vermeil is an older process where the base metal used has to be sterling silver, which is much better for those who have skin allergies to other base metals. The silver is then gold-plated, but with a thicker coating, often as much as 50% thicker than a traditional gold-plated piece. The hands are original antique blued steel. Shown with a black genuine Alligator strap, made in the USA. This watch is a Prototype. It is One-of-a-Kind. All Rpaige watches come with a one year warranty.

watches.name: Convert your Heirloom Pocket watch into a Wrocket watch
watches.description: Convert your heirloom pocket watch to an Rpaige Wrocket watch Do you have an heirloom, or treasured pocket watch, maybe owned and wore by your dad or grandad, and you would love to wear it as a wristwatch? There’s a possibility that it can be converted to an Rpaige Wrocket watch in either steel or Titanium. However,there are limitations and criteria which must be met. The watch must be an Elgin or Waltham, 12 size (approximately 38 mm), and minimum of 15 jewels. See picture for approximate measurements. Note: other American watch manufacturers like Illinois, Hampden, Rockford, Burlington may work in our watches, but the movement (mechanism) must be a Hunter’s case design (the winding stem at the 3 o’clock position). Most Hamilton watches will not fit our cases due to their non-standard sizing. The Rpaige Watch Company will be doing a limited number of these conversions for customers. The conversion includes a complete restoration of the movement, and installing this movement into the Wrocket watch case, either using an Rpaige dial with deco round hands, or the original dial and hands that the pocket watch came as, depending on whether the movement is an open face or hunters case (the winding stem is at the 3 o’clock position). It will come with an Italian Leather Strap with Rpaige Logo on Buckle and strap. $1800 to $2,800 (depending on restoration) Contact us for more info, and price estimation
